Enhancement: NLP to SQL: translate a natural-language question into T-SQL and run it against OHM_CGSScheduler
Feasibility: HIGH for drafting SQL a human reviews; LOW for generate-and-auto-execute. The view is a single denormalised table (16 columns, no joins), which is close to the easiest possible NL2SQL target, so query STRUCTURE will usually be right. Residual risk is value semantics, not structure.
How it works: A model is given the view's schema plus a glossary of what the values mean (Status vocabulary, CompletedDatetime IS NULL = still running, Timeout units, AdHocID/AlertID meaning), and returns a SELECT. The statement is then executed by the existing dmw_run stored process, or pasted into the DMW SQL pane and run by the user.
Short-term demo (current HTML/JS): Add a 7th tab, 'Ask DMW', holding an IFRAME of a Copilot Studio agent published to the Custom Website channel. Prime the agent with the column glossary as knowledge. It returns T-SQL as chat text; the user copies it into the SQL pane and presses Run Query. No API keys, no CORS, no auth plumbing in the page, no change to dmw_run.sas. Fallback with zero licensing: a 'Draft SQL in Copilot' button that copies a pre-built prompt (glossary + question) to the clipboard for pasting into M365 Copilot.
Longer-term approach: Option A (fits existing architecture best): a second stored process, dmw_nl2sql.sas, that calls Azure OpenAI with PROC HTTP, returns the SELECT as JSON, and lets the page show it for confirmation before calling dmw_run. Keeps everything behind the SAS bridge already in place -- no workstation install, no browser CORS. Option B: Fabric Data Agent over SQL Server mirrored into Fabric, tuned with an example-query library. Option C: Power BI Copilot over a semantic model -- generates DAX, not SQL, and resolves the value semantics once at model design time.
Prerequisites: Short term: Copilot Studio licence (Copilot Credits) and permission to publish an agent to a website channel; the column glossary. Long term A: an Azure OpenAI endpoint reachable from the SAS server and PROC HTTP allowed outbound. Long term B: Fabric capacity plus SQL Server mirroring. Long term C: Power BI Premium/Fabric capacity with Copilot enabled.
Key risk / caveat: A wrong query that ERRORS is harmless; a wrong query that returns a plausible number is not. Never auto-execute without review. Note also that 'Execute a SQL query (V2)' is NOT supported over an on-premises data gateway, so the Power Automate generate-and-run pattern has no clean path to A70TUCGSDATA012 -- this is the main reason the long-term options route through SAS, Fabric or Power BI instead.
Rough effort: Demo: 1-2 days once the glossary exists. Long term A: 1-2 weeks. B or C: 4-8 weeks incl. capacity and governance.

Enhancement: Document Q&A: ask questions across a Word document and a repository of other documents (PDF, DOCX, XLSX)
Feasibility: HIGH. This is the most mature capability in the Microsoft stack and needs no change to the database path. Quality depends far more on document hygiene and permissions than on the model.
How it works: Documents are indexed into a vector/semantic index. A question retrieves the most relevant passages, and the model answers from those passages with citations back to the source file. Permissions are enforced at retrieval time, so a user only gets passages from documents they could already open.
Short-term demo (current HTML/JS): Put the document set in a SharePoint library. Build a Copilot Studio agent with that library as its knowledge source, publish it to the Custom Website channel, and embed the IFRAME in a 'Docs' tab beside 'Ask DMW'. Zero-infrastructure variant: an agent builder agent in the M365 Copilot app pointed at the same library -- no embed, but nothing to publish or license beyond M365 Copilot. Start with README.docx and the DMW runbook so the demo answers real support questions.
Longer-term approach: Azure AI Search index over the document repository (vector + semantic ranking, incremental indexing, per-document ACLs) consumed either by Copilot Studio as a knowledge source or by an Azure OpenAI 'on your data' endpoint. Add document-level metadata (system, environment, CR number, effective date) so answers can be filtered and so superseded documents can be excluded rather than silently competing with current ones.
Prerequisites: Short term: a SharePoint library and either M365 Copilot (agent builder) or Copilot Studio (embeddable agent). Long term: Azure AI Search, a storage account or SharePoint as the source of truth, and an agreed metadata/retention scheme.
Key risk / caveat: GOVERNANCE IS THE REAL CONSTRAINT, NOT TECHNOLOGY. Two specific flags: (1) Oversharing -- an agent surfaces anything the asker already has access to, which makes existing loose SharePoint permissions suddenly visible at scale; audit permissions BEFORE indexing. (2) Restricted material -- CMS Transmittal 13870 (CR 14443) states the information is CONFIDENTIAL, may be shared only with A/B MACs, DME MACs and shared system maintainers, and must not be posted to the Internet or Intranet without further instruction from CMS. Do not index that transmittal or its derivatives into any cloud AI index until CMS clearance is confirmed in writing. Keep restricted documents in a separately governed library that the agent is not pointed at.
Rough effort: Demo: 1-3 days. Long term: 3-6 weeks, most of it permissions review and metadata design rather than build.
